title: Marchland
tagline: A conquest game powered by your daily steps, played on one shared map.
about: Your daily step count is the only currency. Each day you claim your steps and spend them to take ground, build castles, towers and walls, and march soldiers across a map shared by every player.

It started as an idea for a land-claiming running game and turned into a small, living strategy game that runs in any browser. The map is relative to each player's castle, so friends who live far apart can still be neighbours.

facts.label: shared by everyone, drawn around each player's castle rather than real geography
no install; a realtime database keeps every player on the same board

board.title: Where it stands
board.intro: Rules and balance change often while the game is being tuned, usually in response to how the players actually play.

nodes.name: Shared map with rivers and bridges
nodes.note: Rivers are hard to cross; a bridge takes a day to build. Rivers get names, and players who hold most of the land around one can rename it.

nodes.name: Daily step claims
nodes.note: Steps are claimed once a day and posted publicly, so other players can dispute a claim.

nodes.name: Castles, towers, walls and roads
nodes.note: Ground only produces when it has a supply path back to a castle. Unmanned structures decay.

nodes.name: Four resources
nodes.note: Stone for walls, timber for castles, iron for soldiers and grain as upkeep.

nodes.name: Soldiers and battles
nodes.note: Battles are probabilistic, and the attack screen shows how many soldiers it takes to reach a 70% chance of winning.

nodes.name: Trebuchets
nodes.note: Siege engines that fire at range, so towers are not unbeatable.

nodes.name: Caravans and letters
nodes.note: Send goods, or a private letter, to another player. Caravans take time to arrive and cost upkeep while they travel.

nodes.name: Tutorial, manual and the Saga
nodes.note: A narrated tutorial, a written manual, and a short cartoon about the realm.

nodes.name: Stronger step verification
nodes.note: Screenshots and public disputes keep claims honest today. A more thorough verification program is planned.

nodes.name: History-themed seasonal events
nodes.note: Ideas under discussion, building on a short October event.

works: Open the game, pick a name and play in any browser.
Watch the manual or the tutorial first if the rules look like a lot; both live on the same site.
Rules changes are announced inside the game.
limits: Steps are self-reported and checked by screenshots and by other players, so the game relies on honest play.
New players join through an existing player who vouches for them.
It is a hobby project, and the rules can change from one week to the next.
source_note: Written from the project's own notes and commit history (latest commit 7 Nov 2026). When the status changes, edit status.json in this folder.
